Why: The promise is the post, not the plan. Amanda announced it on Instagram on 09/19/2026 at 23:00 UTC, post 7213386: "1 true thing about this season, every night from tonight to Halloween. 43 nights. No dark days." 43 is Sep 19 through Oct 31 counting tonight. Nothing in this repo recorded that, so no gate could tell a night the campaign skipped from a night that was simply quiet, and 26 of the 43 went dark without a single check firing. PerNight is 1 because the announcement says 1. It is a floor and a ceiling: 0 breaks the promise, 3 in a day is the month spent in a week. Facebook, TikTok and YouTube carry the same nightly run, and Instagram is the account the words were published on, which is why PromisedOn is narrower than Accounts.
WhyCountdown: 1 true fact a night from the trailer date to Halloween. The trailers state the number of nights left, so the number is only true on the day the post is scheduled. Inclusive means tonight is night 1, which is how the trailers were written. Moving a trailer changes its number, which is what C04 is for.
WhyStart: StartDate was 2026-09-19 until 09/30. The run that is actually live starts 2026-09-29 and is 33 nights, and 2 things in this repo say so first hand: halloween-33/approval/plan.json holds 33 rows, night 1 dated 2026-09-29, and the 4 posts that published on the night of 09/29 carry the line Night 1 of 33 in their own captions, live on instagram 45886, tiktok 41488, facebook 30840 and youtube 36129. The 43 in the Announcement column is still exactly what was published on 09/19 and is left alone, because what a campaign promised out loud is data. The 2 numbers are 2 different facts: 43 nights was announced when the trailer went out 10 days early, and the run was then rebuilt as 33 from 09/29. Conflating them is what had C13 measuring a live promise against a window that started 10 nights before the campaign did. Amanda should sanity check this line, because it is a correction made from the repo's own data rather than from her.
WhyHorizon: 5, which is 2 less than the loader's own --days 7, and the 2 are not a mistake. load.py places a night when its slot time falls inside now plus 7 days. The campaign's slots are 23:00 and 23:30, and the workflow runs at midday, so a run on day D0 reaches the 23:00 slot on D0 plus 6 and not the one on D0 plus 7. This nightly check runs at about 01:00, before the day's load, so the newest run it can see is yesterday's: D0 is the day before the board opens, and the reach is the board's first day plus 5. Measured on 09/30: run 10 loaded on 09/29 and placed night 7 on 10/05, which is 09/30 plus 5 exactly. Being 1 night conservative is the right way round. A gate that names a night the loader is about to fill anyway gets switched off, and a gate 1 night late still catches a dark night 5 nights before it happens. The version of this that needs no arithmetic is the loader writing its own window where the gate can read it, instead of only into its run log.
